name: Narragansett Bay Commission - Field's Point WWTF and associated CSOs
outfalls_source: https://cso-api.narrabay.com/pins (OF 004-067 with lat/long); RIGIS https://services2.arcgis.com/S8zZg9pg23JUEexQ/arcgis/rest/services/UTILITY_NBC_Sewer_Overflows_spf/FeatureServer/0
notification_channel: NBC CSO Alarm Map, https://www.narrabay.com/programs-and-initiatives/combined-sewer-overflow-cso/cso-alarm-map/ (JSON: https://cso-api.narrabay.com/pins and /dryoverflows). Red dot = overflow in last 24 h, orange = last 48 h. No email/text sign-up found. 'Report an overflow' email IMSupport@narrabay.com. 2017 permit required 'a system to provide web-based notification to the public on CSO occurrences'.
notes: 35 CSO outfalls with coordinates in the NBC API for the Field's Point system (plus plant outfall OF 002 FP, one abandoned site and a test site); 9 of them say 'No data available' (no live alarm). NBC states 64 active CSO pipes district-wide. Phase I tunnel (2008) captures flow from 12 FP-area CSOs. Permit administratively continued (expired 2022-11-30 per ECHO/RISE). Receiving-water assignment per outfall is inferred from site names and coordinates (see raw/nbc-outfalls-from-api.csv). Woonasquatucket, Moshassuck and West rivers have no openboatlaunch slug.

name: Narragansett Bay Commission - Bucklin Point WWTF and associated CSOs
outfalls_source: https://cso-api.narrabay.com/pins (OF 101-107, 201-220); RIGIS UTILITY_NBC_Sewer_Overflows_spf
notification_channel: NBC CSO Alarm Map, https://www.narrabay.com/programs-and-initiatives/combined-sewer-overflow-cso/cso-alarm-map/ (JSON: https://cso-api.narrabay.com/pins and /dryoverflows). Same map as Field's Point. Dry-weather CSOs also appear in EPA ECHO as violations.
notes: 25 CSO outfalls in the API for this system (1 without live data: OF 211). Phase III (RestoredWaters RI) Pawtucket Tunnel (2.2 mi to Bucklin Point) excavated by Feb 2024; in-service date not confirmed. ECHO 2026: dry-weather CSO 08/17/2026 and 10/05-06/2026, dry-weather bypass 03/23/2026; annual sewer-event total 2 events / 506,410 gal. Pawtucket and Central Falls own their local combined sewers but the CSO outfalls are permitted to NBC.

name: City of Newport Utilities - Water Pollution Control (WPCF and two CSO treatment facilities)
outfalls_source: https://utilities.newportri.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Sewer-System-Overview-Map.pdf (map; not machine-readable); FAQ: Wellington Ave CSO outfall 'north east of the Ida Lewis Rock'; Washington Street CSO outfall 'east of the north end of Goat Island'
notification_channel: Red flag raised at the CSO facility when an overflow starts, kept up 'until 24 hours after the overflow stops'; red flag also at the Harbormaster's Building. CSO events reported to RIDEM and EPA. 'Summary of CSO Events since 2001' PDF linked from the CSO FAQ. City emergency alert system for general utility notices (not CSO-specific). Live harbor sondes on NexSens WQData LIVE (https://www.wqdatalive.com/public/2461, unreachable on check).
notes: Two CSO facilities (Wellington Avenue CSO Treatment Facility, Washington Street CSO Treatment Facility) disinfect overflow before discharge. Consent Decree with EPA and RIDEM. Permit administratively continued (expired 2020-05-31). ECHO: wet-weather bypass 03/06/2026 (83,456 gal 2026 total); 2024 1,134,900 gal.

name: East Providence Wastewater Treatment Facility (City of East Providence)
outfalls_source: RIDEM RISE GIS 'Waste Water Treatment Facility Discharge' layer https://risegis.ri.gov/hosting/rest/services/RIDEM/Regulated_Facilities/FeatureServer/24 (plant points only; collection-system overflow points are not published)
notification_channel: No public notification channel found. Operator must report SSOs/bypasses to RIDEM verbally (as soon as possible, within 24 h) and electronically via EPA NeT-SewerOverflow within 5 calendar days; those reports surface later in EPA ECHO detailed facility reports. Public hears only if DEM closes shellfish areas (hotline 401-222-2900, Constant Contact email list, dem.ri.gov/shellfish, sometimes a press release) or RIDOH/DEM issue a contact advisory.
notes: May 4, 2026 force-main break: ~800,000 gal to Watchemoket Cove/Providence River; DEM press release next day closed shellfish Area 16E. ECHO 2024: 4 bypass events, 174,000 gal. ecoRI reports ~30,000 ft of 'critically defective' pipe.
